punchline: Bill Gates opened a jar of mosquitoes on the TED stage, and the room remembered his malaria talk.
thirty_sec: In 2009 Bill Gates spoke at TED about malaria and opened a jar of mosquitoes on stage. The Gates Foundation later said they were not carrying the disease. Carmine Gallo uses it as his example of a jaw-dropping moment, one that took under five percent of an eighteen-minute talk. His advice is that every presentation needs one such moment.
